stories.head: InMobi Launches Agentic AI Advertising Platform with Seven Specialized Agents
stories.plain: InMobi Accelerate deploys seven specialized AI agents that autonomously plan, build, launch, and optimize campaigns across Google, Meta, TikTok, Microsoft, and ChatGPT Ads. This matters because it shifts media buying from a human-driven workflow to an agentic decisioning loop, lowering the bar for smaller businesses and agencies to run omnichannel advertising without large ops teams.

stories.head: Marketing-Specific AI Guardrails Are Needed Beyond Enterprise Governance
stories.plain: Enterprise-wide AI governance policies are too broad to catch off-brand or legally risky marketing content before it goes public. The piece argues that marketing teams need their own layer of AI guardrails — tone, compliance, brand voice — sitting on top of corporate policy. Practically, this shapes how martech stacks must be bought and configured going forward.

stories.head: Impact.com: 92% of AI-Active Shoppers Buy AI-Recommended Products, But Most Finish Purchase Off-Platform
stories.plain: New research finds 92% of AI-active US consumers have purchased an AI-recommended product, yet only 31% completed the transaction inside the AI tool — 55% left to finish at a retailer. This gap signals a critical attribution and conversion problem for marketers building strategies around AI-driven discovery and generative engine optimization.

stories.head: ZoomInfo Launches Sales Plugin for ChatGPT Work, Bringing GTM Data into AI Chat
stories.plain: ZoomInfo's new ChatGPT Work plugin lets sellers build prospect lists, find in-market accounts, and enrich data without leaving the chat interface. This is a meaningful product change — it embeds live B2B data directly into an AI reasoning environment, accelerating the shift toward agentic sales workflows where the AI both retrieves intelligence and suggests next actions.

stories.head: Forrester's Charles Betz: AI Agent Autonomy Is a Risk Design Choice, Not a Maturity Milestone
stories.plain: Forrester analyst Charles Betz reframes the debate: giving an AI agent more autonomy is a deliberate risk decision, not a sign of technical progress. He outlines what guardrails and audit infrastructure must exist before autonomy is expanded. For anyone buying or governing agentic martech, this is a practical framework that challenges vendor hype around autonomous agents.

stories.head: Bloomreach Acquires AEO Leader AthenaHQ to Connect AI Visibility to Revenue
stories.plain: Bloomreach, a major customer engagement platform, bought AthenaHQ, which specialises in answer engine optimisation — getting brands surfaced inside AI-generated answers. The deal signals that GEO is now a board-level revenue topic, not just an SEO experiment, and that CEPs are racing to own the measurement link between AI discovery and actual sales.

stories.head: InMobi Launches Agentic AI Advertising Platform with Seven Specialised Campaign Agents
stories.plain: InMobi Accelerate deploys seven AI agents that plan, build, launch, and optimise omnichannel campaigns across Google, Meta, TikTok, Microsoft and ChatGPT Ads without human hand-holding. This is a concrete example of agentic decisioning moving from enterprise pilots to self-serve tools available to smaller businesses and agencies, changing how ad budgets get managed.

stories.head: Twilio Adds Hallucination Detection and Task Completion Scoring for AI Agents
stories.plain: Twilio released two new Conversation Intelligence operators in public beta: one flags AI hallucinations in agent replies, the other scores whether the agent actually finished its task. These are the first measurable quality controls built directly into a major CEP, making AI agent governance a shipping feature rather than a policy document.

stories.head: Forrester Analyst: AI Agent Autonomy Is a Design Choice, Not a Maturity Level
stories.plain: Forrester's Charles Betz argues that how much autonomy you give an AI agent should be driven by risk tolerance, not by chasing a maturity score. He lays out a practical framework for running AI experiments that actually teach you something before you expand agent authority — directly relevant to anyone buying or governing agentic tools.

stories.head: adMarketplace Data: AI Search Conversion Rates Up 156%, But Intent Varies Sharply by Platform
stories.plain: A full year of live data from adMarketplace shows conversion rates 156% higher in AI-powered search experiences, but also that shoppers behave very differently across browsers, comparison engines and BNPL apps. The finding matters for media planners: AI search is not one channel, and treating it as such will misallocate budget.

themes.head: AI Agents Are Reshaping the Buyer Journey Before Marketers Are Ready
body: AI agents are increasingly making or heavily influencing purchase decisions on behalf of consumers and B2B buyers, as evidenced by impact.com research showing 92% of AI-active shoppers buy AI-recommended products. This means the audience a marketer must persuade is no longer purely human — it includes the agent doing the shortlisting.

The strategic implication is profound: traditional brand signals like ad creative and landing-page copy matter less if an agent never surfaces your brand in the first place. Bloomreach's acquisition of AEO specialist AthenaHQ signals that AI Engine Optimization is becoming as essential as SEO, and vendors who ignore agent-readable signals risk disappearing from consideration entirely.

themes.head: Agentic AI Demands Governance Before Autonomy
body: Forrester's Charles Betz and multiple industry voices are issuing a consistent warning: granting AI agents more autonomy does not equal greater maturity. Organizations are deploying agents faster than they can define success metrics, accountability structures, or rollback procedures — a gap that creates compounding risk as agents touch customer-facing workflows.

Twilio's new hallucination-detection and task-completion scoring tools, and enterprise governance frameworks from Digital.ai, reflect a market response to this gap. Marketers need observable, auditable agent behavior as a prerequisite — not an afterthought — before handing over campaign execution or customer conversations to autonomous systems.

themes.head: ChatGPT Becomes an Advertising & Sales Surface
body: Within a single news cycle, Pinewood.AI added a ChatGPT ads channel to its Boost tool and ZoomInfo launched sales plugin extensions for ChatGPT via GTM.AI. Conversational AI interfaces are no longer just content tools — they are emerging media placements where brands can intercept buyer intent in a genuinely new context.

This compresses the traditional funnel: a buyer asking ChatGPT for vendor recommendations can receive a sponsored answer, click through, and be enriched with ZoomInfo data before reaching a sales rep. Marketers need to decide now how to allocate budget and creative strategy for this channel before it matures and CPMs spike.

themes.head: Brand Reputation Faces AI-Era Blind Spots
body: Multiple pieces this month converge on a single warning: internal AI governance policies cannot fully protect a brand when the threats originate from third-party models, AI-generated misinformation, or agent-mediated discovery that surfaces competitors ahead of you. Reputation risk has expanded well beyond owned channels.

The practical response requires monitoring how AI systems describe and represent your brand externally, not just auditing your own AI outputs. Real-time personalization must also be balanced against consumer trust — over-targeting or opaque data use can erode the brand equity that AI-driven acquisition is meant to build.

MarTech · protect brand reputation in AI era

themes.head: Measurement Must Catch Up to AI-First Media
body: As AI reshapes media buying, creative production, and channel mix simultaneously, legacy attribution models break down. Building a cross-channel measurement framework designed for AI-first media — one that accounts for agent-driven discovery, conversational ad placements, and AI-generated creative variants — has moved from best practice to urgent priority.

The warning that cheap CAC can mask expensive long-term growth problems reinforces this: optimizing for short-term conversion signals in AI-managed campaigns can destroy lifetime value and brand health metrics that only appear in longer measurement windows. Marketers who set up the right measurement infrastructure now will have a durable competitive advantage.
ev: MarTech · deploying agents faster than measuring

month.takeaway: The defining tension of this moment is that AI is simultaneously the new media surface, the new buyer, and the new execution layer — and most marketing organizations have measurement, governance, and brand-visibility strategies built for none of those three roles.
